name: Sabey Data Centers Ashburn - Building C

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This Sabey Data Centers facility is part of SDC Ashburn in Virginia, one of the company seven current data center campuses alongside sites in Austin Texas, East Wenatchee and Seattle Washington, Manhattan New York, and Umatilla Oregon. Sabey own site states Sabey Data Centers was established in 2010 as a partnership between Sabey Corporation and investor National Real Estate Advisors. Sabey Corporation itself was founded in 1972 as a commercial real estate developer under founder Dave Sabey. The company data center business originated in Seattle during the dot com collapse when a vacated tenant building became SDC Seattle, building 5, prompting the pivot into data centers. Sabey Data Centers now operates six data center campuses nationally encompassing more than 3.5 million square feet developed over twenty years. No building specific address, opening date, or individual MW figures for the Ashburn campus specifically were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Sabey Data Centers' Ashburn Building C delivers 54 MW of IT capacity, ranking sixth among Virginia facilities with published power figures and representing roughly 4 percent of the 1,326 MW total across the state's 19 disclosed data center sites.

The 54 MW ceiling constrains what hardware density this building can support. At 40 kW per rack, a typical density for GPU training, this translates to approximately 1,350 racks. At 10 kW per rack, a conservative estimate for general colocation, the same power supports roughly 5,400 racks. The operator publishes no rack count, cooling architecture, or cabinet power density, so whether this facility prioritizes dense AI compute or lighter enterprise workloads cannot be determined from available data.

The facility holds certifications for financial controls (SOC 1 Type 2), security and availability standards (SOC 2 Type 2), payment card compliance (PCI DSS), healthcare data (HIPAA), and information security management (ISO 27001), with SSAE 18 as the attestation foundation. These qualify Building C for regulated enterprise and government workloads beyond hyperscale training. The operator does not disclose tenant identity or workload composition. Virginia's 326 mapped facilities show that most publish no capacity figure, making individual building contributions to state compute infrastructure largely invisible.
